jobs.occupation: Staff Scientist in RNA biology and metabolite RNA capping (re-posting)
jobs.description:
The Department of Biology is looking for a highly motivated and independent Staff Scientist in RNA biology and metabolite RNA capping. The position is expected to commence on 1 January 2027 and is linked to the Lundbeck Foundation Experiment grant MINDtheCAP: A new role of RNA caps in intellectual disability.

  Our research
 The Section for Computational and RNA Biology combines experimental and computational approaches to investigate RNA biology, gene regulation and genome-wide molecular processes. The position will be anchored in the Vinther research group and will contribute to the section's research activities, collaborations and supervision environment.

  Your job
 The Staff Scientist will have scientific responsibility for the day-to-day implementation of MINDtheCAP and will independently plan and coordinate the work within the project's objectives, milestones, budget and reporting requirements.

   	
• Plan, prioritise and carry out the project in accordance with its scientific objectives, milestones, budget and reporting requirements. 	
• Analyse and interpret high-throughput sequencing and molecular data and refine the associated bioinformatic workflows. 	
• Coordinate project activities with laboratory technical staff and internal and external collaborators, and supervise students or junior researchers where relevant. 	
• Maintain research documentation and data-management practices and ensure compliance with laboratory safety, research-integrity and relevant institutional requirements. 	
• Prepare scientific publications, conference presentations, seminars, workshops, grant reports and relevant outreach activities. 	
• Develop follow-up research directions, collaborations and applications for further competitive research funding.   Because the work is research-driven, its detailed timing and sequence cannot be fully predetermined. Within the agreed scientific and institutional framework, the Staff Scientist will independently determine day-to-day priorities, experimental design and methods, the sequencing of experiments and analyses, and the coordination of collaborations.

  Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic Staff Scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Qualifications and Expectations 

   	
• A master’s degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, RNA biology or a closely related field. 	
• Interest in and/or experience with RNA biology, RNA capping or RNA biochemistry. 	
• Experience with molecular biology techniques and laboratory work. Experience developing and optimising RNA-related methods, sequencing-library preparation and quantitative experimental controls is considered an advantage. 	
• Experience with or interest in analysing and interpreting transcriptomic data and in using or developing bioinformatic workflows. 	
• Interest in data analysis and bioinformatics. Experience with bioinformatic tools or workflows is considered an advantage. 	
• Experience preparing scientific reports, manuscripts and presentations is an advantage. Previous scientific publications are considered an advantage.  	
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a research environment within agreed milestones and budgets. 	
• Good written and oral communication skills in English.   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Experience managing externally funded research projects and contributing to competitive funding applications. 	
• Experience coordinating interdisciplinary collaborations and working with molecular or neuronal cell-model systems. 	
• Experience supervising students, junior researchers or technical staff. 	
• Ability to work independently, solve scientific and technical challenges, and collaborate effectively across disciplines.   Place of employment
 The place of employment is the Section for Computational and RNA Biology, Department of Biology, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment, with access to facilities and expertise in RNA biochemistry, molecular biology, high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatics.

  Terms of employment

  The average weekly working time is 37 hours.

  The position is fixed-term for two years, from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2028.

  The position is classified as Staff Scientist (AC-TAP). Employment will be under The Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). The monthly salary will be based on the number of years of work experience (seniority) and there will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). The applicable pension contribution will be in accordance with the relevant collective agreement.

  Application
 If you are interested in the position, please submit your electronic application, including attachments, via the UCPH Job Portal (click the “Apply for position” link at the bottom of the job posting).

  Your application should be submitted in English and include:

   	
• A letter of application addressing the requirements, maximum one page. 	
• Curriculum vitae. 	
• A certified or signed copy of certificate(s) of education.   The application deadline is 9 November 2026

  Interviews are expected to be held shortly after the application deadline.

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Jeppe Vinther at jvinther@bio.ku.dk.
  

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

  The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative organizational structure, which is currently being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and the development of, among other things, workflows and interfaces for collaboration.

• An MSc or PhD in life sciences, or a related discipline, with relevant experience in drug discovery or development.

As Sr AI Process Designer in Rapid Enablement, you will help business areas across Novo rethink how work gets done with AI, rather than simply applying AI to what already exists. By designing future-state services around what AI and people each do well, and testing them with real users, you help the right ideas move forward fast.

What you’ll bring

You are proactive and structured, able to frame ambiguous problems independently, challenge an initial solution request constructively, and test a better future state under time pressure. You bring most of the following:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in service design, interaction design, human-computer interaction or a related field.

• 4+ years of experience applying service design, human-centred design or closely related methods to complex services or business processes, including researching and mapping end-to-end processes across multiple actors, systems, channels and organisational boundaries.

• Strong facilitation experience, including online and in-person creative workshops and co-design sessions with senior, multidisciplinary stakeholders.

• The ability to turn research and operational evidence into clear design opportunities and future-state services, and to prototype and test concepts iteratively rather than relying only on analysis and documentation.

• Excellent visual and verbal communication skills: you make complex processes understandable to non-design and technical audiences, and challenge existing ways of working with confidence.

• A pragmatic mindset: good today is better than perfect tomorrow. You balance great user experiences with project constraints.

• Strong planning and project management skills, with the ability to own larger deliverables independently and translate strategy into ambitious, testable goals.

• Comfort working at pace with incomplete information, and strong collaboration skills with business subject-matter experts, software engineers and AI specialists.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience redesigning knowledge-work or enterprise business processes.

• AI-enabled service or workflow design, including human-in-the-loop patterns.

• Experience in enterprise transformation, internal consulting, or regulated and highly complex organisations.

• Designing services that span digital and non-digital interactions.

• Experience with experimentation, rapid prototyping and discovery methods, and connecting design decisions to measurable business value.

Deep AI expertise is not required. You do need to understand the possibilities and limitations of AI well enough to design effectively alongside technical colleagues.

What you’ll do

You will work in short iterations and test the riskiest unknowns first, making quick progress while reducing risk. You will facilitate the process from start to finish, bring others along without formal authority, and share findings so decision makers can act.

• Work with team members and stakeholders to make hypotheses concrete through journey maps, service blueprints and prototypes.

• Test concepts with users and stakeholders, use the evidence to iterate, and help decide whether to proceed, change direction or stop.

• Capture rationale and evidence so a receiving team can continue the work after Rapid Enablement exits.

The team exists to rapidly accelerate high-value AI opportunities across the Novo value chain, from idea to an evidence-based proof of value, and to build reusable enterprise productivity agents.

In cross-functional engagements, you will work with business stakeholders, process owners, engineers and AI specialists. Together you will move from a first request to a clear decision on what should happen next, with a direct effect on how AI improves workflows and is adopted across Novo.

What you can expect here

You will work at the leading edge of how Novo turns AI ambition into proven, adopted solutions, with your design judgement directly shaping which opportunities move forward. You will operate independently on ambiguous, high-value problems and receive guidance mainly on the most complex issues.

Each engagement touches a different part of the value chain, so you will build new skills and broaden your view of the business while contributing your expertise from day one. As Laboratory Technician in Research Bioanalysis, you will help early-stage research projects get the answers they need. You will develop and run immunoassays that measure proteins and peptides in biological samples, giving project teams data to predict how long new compounds stay in circulation and how they work in the body. Your work supports early research in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular diseases.

What you’ll bring

• A relevant education in laboratory technology or equivalent.

• Proficiency in general biological research laboratory techniques and workflows.

• Practical experience analysing biological samples.

• A keen interest in data analysis and a drive to keep data quality high.

• A flair for IT and laboratory instruments, with the willingness to learn and adapt.

• A proactive attitude towards building your analytical technical skills, with an open mindset.

• An energetic, self-driven and organised way of working, and a team-player mindset.

• Hands-on experience with immunoassays such as ELISA, MSD or AlphaLISA.

What you’ll do

New projects often call for new ways of measuring different proteins and peptides. You will spend a significant part of your time developing tailored methods, alongside analysing samples with established ones.

• Develop and implement new immunoassays for the proteins and peptides your collaborators need to measure.

• Analyse samples from in vivo and in vitro studies using immunoassays

• Plan and carry out sample analyses, using robotics and IT systems to handle samples efficiently and track data.

• Proactively improve laboratory workflows and integrate new digital tools and AI

Curiosity, data, technology and collaboration come together to help meet future health needs.

Your team is high-achieving, multidisciplinary and international: seven laboratory technicians, one tech trainee, four associate scientists and eight scientists. You will also work with collaborators who provide the samples and rely on your data, and with colleagues in other departments as workflows are refined across the research process.

You will work in a department that is putting automation, digital tools and AI to use in everyday analytical work. You will have room to build new technical skills, take ownership of method development and make your voice heard on how the work is done.
